### Revision r2652 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **THE STATE-FIXER HAS ITS OWN THRESHOLD at $\Gamma=-1/4$, and r2651's operator crosses it.**

**⌗ THE MECHANISM.** *P10: "**Thermal (Hartle--Hawking) regularity is Euclidean smoothness at the horizon mode by
mode**" — imposing the regular branch $x^{1/2+\nu}$, $\nu=\sqrt{\hat\Gamma+\tfrac14}$, on each sub-threshold
fibre, the surface gravity being "**common to every fibre**".*

**⛭⛭ BUT $\nu$ IS REAL ONLY FOR $\Gamma\ge-1/4$:**

    Gamma =  0.75 -> nu = 1.00      limit-point, no condition needed
    Gamma = -0.24 -> nu = 0.10      branch selectable
    Gamma = -0.26 -> nu IMAGINARY   no regular branch exists

⇒ ***Below $-1/4$ both exponents go complex, $x^{1/2\pm i|\nu|}$ oscillates infinitely as $x\to0$, and **neither
branch is regular — there is nothing for thermal regularity to select**. And $-1/4$ is the classical
**fall-to-the-centre** threshold, not an artefact.***
⇒⇒ ***And r2651's operator reaches $-47.8$ on attainable $(\pi,\phi)$. The two results meet.***

**⌗ SO `PO-6`'s SUCCESSOR QUESTION SHARPENS** *from the open-ended "what fixes the state?" to the determinate:*
***does the interacting dynamics keep $\hat\Gamma$ above $-1/4$ on the states it actually realises, or does the
sub-$(-1/4)$ region carry support?***
⌗⌗ ***And that is a question about the MEASURE on the tower — this row's other half. Third time this session a row's
two remaining halves turned out to be one question from two ends.***

**⛭ THE RULE:** ***when a result opens a successor question, check whether the corpus's existing answer to that
question has a DOMAIN. A mechanism stated without its range of validity reads as universal — and the range is
usually the first thing a new result violates.***

⚠ *An oscillatory endpoint still admits a one-parameter family of extensions. **What is lost is the canonical one —
and with it "closed without a free parameter", which is what the free-sector argument earns.***

### Revision r2651 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **`PO-6`'s FLOOR QUESTION ANSWERED — NO, at the order the paper names.**

**⌗ THE QUESTION, narrowed to one thing at r2619:** *does the completed $\hat\Gamma$ keep a floor? P10 leaves it
open in its own voice — and **names exactly what enters**: "At leading order
$\hat\Gamma=\gamma+c\sum_n\hat\pi_n^2$; but **the cubic and higher self-interactions enter at the same
inverse-square order at the origin ($\pi_n^2\phi_m/a^3$ in kind)**".*

**⛭⛭ AND THE STRUCTURE DECIDES IT.** *Grouped, $\hat\Gamma=\gamma+\hat\pi^2(c+g_3\hat\phi)$ — where
$\hat\pi^2$ is a **square** and $\hat\phi$ is a **signed field amplitude**.*
⇒ ***The coefficient of $\pi^2$ turns negative wherever $\phi<-c/g_3$, and $\hat\Gamma\to-\infty$ as $\pi^2$
grows.*** *(Sampled over 200,000 points at $\gamma=0.25$, $c=g_3=1$: minimum $-209$.)*
⇒⇒ ***So the leading-order "sum of squares" is destroyed by the FIRST correction — the correction is not a square
but a square times a signed field.***

**⌗ AND THE PAPER BUILT ITS DECOMPOSITION NOT TO NEED IT:** *"uses only that both sides of the threshold are
occupied, **and not that the spectrum has a floor**".*
⇒ ***That reads as modesty until the floor fails; then it reads as foresight. A construction arranged so nothing
rests on an open question is not hedging — it is the shape of an argument built by someone who suspected the
answer.***

**⛭ THE RULE:** ***when a paper marks a property as "not assumed here", ask whether the property is TRUE before
assuming the caution was routine. The most informative caveats are written by an author who could see how it would
go.***

⚠ *The vein stays dark: **what remains is not the floor but what fixes the STATE** — an operator unbounded below is
a standard situation, and the question changes rather than closing. `L-165` narrowed **12×**.*

**⛭ THE RULE:** ***when a corpus establishes that "the ratio cancels", find out WHICH ratio. A cancellation is a
statement about what two things share, and two quantities can both be ratios while sharing nothing — the word
carries none of the structure that does the work.***

*· **INSTRUMENT** — a tool, ledger or gate built to run the work better.*

recorded. And build it so it refuses to move for a rewrite — a metric you can improve by editing prose is a metric
measuring your prose.***

about whether the work can START.***

wrongly. Run it on the new population before trusting it — the ranking that looks absurd is the one telling you what
the score actually means.***

working record stays out of the papers.***

the prose binds** (a claim deleted with its receipt fails nothing) · **rehome, do not annotate** · de-narrate by the
tense test · ⛭ ***follow the cross-references*** · update the ledger with reasoning · **update `PROTECTED_OPEN` on
PROGRESS, not only on closure** · regenerate and gate.*

no first step.***
⇒⇒ ***NOT "$T=0$" — THE MECHANISM IS ABSENT.***

### Revision r2494 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **THE KNOT IS UNTIED — item 23 answered, `L-203` STRUCK, and four objects turn out to have been sharing one word.**

**⌗⌗ THE RULE THAT SETTLES IT:** ***a connected cover's deck group acts FREELY on each fibre, so its order divides
the degree — and equals the degree only if the cover is NORMAL.***

| object | monodromy | deck | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| the **3-sheeted cover** of the $2M$-plane | $S_3$ | ***TRIVIAL*** | *non-normal: $\lvert S_3\rvert=6\ne3$* |
| the **cube-root cover** $w^3=z$ | $\mathbb Z_3$ | $\mathbb Z_3$ | *normal, acts regularly* |
| the **GALOIS CLOSURE**, degree 6 | $S_3$ | $S_3$ | ***the "degree-six dial"*** |
| the **equianharmonic curve** $y^2=x^3+1$ | — | $\mathrm{Aut}=\mathbb Z_6$ | *not a cover of the plane* |

*The horizon cubic is irreducible over $\mathbb Q(M)$ with discriminant $-4(27M^2-1)$, not a square in
$\mathbb C(2M)$, **so its Galois group is the full $S_3$** — and a degree-3 cover is normal iff its monodromy has
order 3.* ⇒ ***Six is not three, so the three-sheeted cover's deck group is trivial.***

**⇒⇒ SO EACH TEXT IS RIGHT ABOUT A DIFFERENT COVER AND NOTHING IN THE CORPUS IS WRONG.** *`prop:deck`'s $S_3$ is the
**monodromy** of the three-sheeted cover **and** the **deck** of the closure — both true, so ***the heading names the
wrong COVER, not the wrong GROUP***. `rem:equianharmonic`'s $\mathbb Z_3$ is the deck of the cube-root cover, also
correct.*

**⛭⛭ AND THE RULE THIS EARNS:** ***a word attached to the wrong object looks exactly like a wrong word, and the two
have different repairs — one RENAMES, the other DISAMBIGUATES.*** *Node 23's own fix ("the word is monodromy") is
true and **loses information**; **saying which cover is true and adds it**.*
⌗ *And the diagnostic is cheap: ***if each use of the contested word is correct about SOMETHING, you have an object
count and not a vocabulary error*** — the tell being that the "wrong" statements keep turning out defensible, which
happened three times here.*

**⌗ AND IT EXPLAINS `L-203`'s CONVERGENCE.** ***Its three stations were not three fields finding one error. They
were three fields each noticing that four objects shared one name*** *— and convergence on a NAMING collision is
exactly what you would expect when the underlying mathematics is right.*
⇒ *It also discharges what Ⓗ and Ⓖ were waiting on: P14's **"the Weyl $S_3$ IS the relation among the three
hinges"** names the monodromy, so **the equivariant index is equivariant under $S_3$ and $\mathrm{ad}(P)$ is built
from the same $S_3$**. ***The group question is settled; what remains for Ⓗ is the computation.***

carry ONE mass parameter**."* ⇒ **One $2M$ → three roots → three hinges → three walls.**
⇒⇒ ***THE BASE IS THE $2M$-PLANE AND THE FIBRE IS THE THREE ROOTS. THAT IS THE ROOT COVER*** — *`C1`/`C3`'s object:
three-sheeted, branched at the two Nariai values, monodromy $S_3$, deck trivial, Galois closure the degree-six dial.*

### Revision r2450 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **`L-207` ⓵ DISCHARGED — the general inhomogeneous leaf is EXHIBITED, and the exhibit is the corpus's own coordinate system.**

**⌗⌗ WHAT WAS OWED, and W1 had left it precisely.** *r2424 established that P8's general inhomogeneous evolution is
**not a missing generative law** — "ordinary dynamical evolution of the leaf" — and that the row's "deepest open
question the construction RAISES" framing came from a `%` comment. **But W1 said what it had not done:** "the
general inhomogeneous case is called ordinary **without being EXHIBITED**. The open item is an EXHIBITION, not a
DISCOVERY."*

**⛭ THE EXHIBIT IS LEMAÎTRE–TOLMAN–BONDI WITH $\Lambda$, and it is not an import.** *The general spherically
symmetric inhomogeneous dust, carrying an **arbitrary mass function $m(r)$** — genuinely inhomogeneous rather than a
perturbation — and* ***P2's cycloid IS an LTB interior***: *"the Schwarzschild interior in Lemaître–Tolman
coordinates has areal radius $r(z)=M(1+\cos z)$." **The construction's own coordinates, carrying a general matter
distribution.***

**⌗ BOTH HALVES COMPUTED FROM THE METRIC HERE, not quoted.**
*· **The bend-density identity is EXACT for arbitrary $m(r)$:** $G_{tt}-\Lambda = 2m'(r)/(R^2R')$, which is P8's
$\rho = m'/4\pi R^2R'$ **with no condition on $m$** — and **$E(r)$ drops out of the density entirely**.*
⇒ ***The slicing operator's kinematic identity does not weaken as the matter is made inhomogeneous.***
*· **And the evolution is ordinary GR with no extra law:** the constraint $\dot R^2 = 2m/R + 2E + \Lambda R^2/3$
differentiates to* **$\ddot R = -m(r)/R^2 + \Lambda R/3$** *— **the same equation the homogeneous case obeys**, with
$m$ and $E$ now functions of $r$, and* ***no term coupling different shells.***

**⇒ SO THE EXHIBITION IS THIS:** ***the general inhomogeneous leaf evolves by ONE equation per comoving shell; the
shells do not talk to each other; and the inhomogeneity enters ONLY as the $r$-dependence of two free functions.***

**⌗⌗ AND THE POINT, stated so it is not overread:** ***NOTHING FIXES $m(r)$ IN GENERAL RELATIVITY EITHER — it is
initial data, not a law's output.*** ⇒ **So the construction owes no generative law for the curve for exactly the
reason GR owes none:** *the theory says **how a given matter distribution evolves**, not **which one obtains**. The
bend-density identity converts between the curve and the density; the evolution is GR's, unchanged; and the free
functions are initial data in both.*

⚠ *Not claimed: that LTB exhausts the general case — it is spherically symmetric dust and the general case is
neither.* ***What is exhibited is that the SPECIFIC WORRY — that genuine inhomogeneity might require a generative
law the kinematic operator cannot supply — does not arise where it can be checked exactly.***

⌗ **This closes the third and last of W1's three instances:** *the confined case was exhibited in P11 (the

### Revision r2447 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **A BLIND RUN ANSWERS `L-230`'s INSTRUMENT QUESTION IN THE NEGATIVE — inconsistency and overreach are opposite signatures, and no instrument sees both.**

**⌗⌗ THE RUN.** *`scope_table`, sharpened at r2446, taken across all seventeen papers with no prior.* ⇒ ***Every flag
is in P15. Not one in P01–P14, P16 or P17 — and P14 shows NOTHING, because after the string-literal fix its `M` has
a single setting, 0.12.***

**⚠⚠ SO THE TOOL CANNOT SEE `F14`, THE STRONGEST MEMBER OF THE CLASS IT WAS ADOPTED FOR — and the reason is
structural rather than a tuning failure.** *`scope_table` measures **DISAGREEMENT between receipts**. `F14`'s defect
is **AGREEMENT**: every P14 receipt runs at $M=0.12$, and **the paper generalises from that single value**.*
⇒ ***INCONSISTENCY IS MANY VALUES WHERE ONE IS CLAIMED; OVERREACH IS ONE VALUE WHERE MANY ARE CLAIMED. An instrument
tuned to the first is blind to the second by construction, and no sharpening crosses that.***

**⌗ AND THE GENERAL FORM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE INSTANCE, so it is filed as a scrap:** ***before adopting an
instrument for a class, ask what the class's SIGNATURE is in the data the instrument reads.*** *Here the class's
signature was **uniformity**, and the tool was a **variance detector**. That was decidable before the adoption and
was not asked.*

**⌗ SO `L-230`'s CLASS HAS TWO HALVES, and the tool serves the one it was not adopted for.**
*· **overreach** — signature *agreement* — ⛔ **no instrument, and `scope_table` structurally cannot**;*
*· **inconsistency** — signature *disagreement* — ✔ `scope_table`, whose real yield is `F15`'s two parameter sets.*
***That is receipt-layer CONSISTENCY, which is worth having and is a different thing from scope.***

**⇒ AND THE ROUTE THAT REMAINS IS ONE THE CORPUS ALREADY INVENTED.** *Detecting overreach means comparing a
receipt's scope against **the sentence's quantifier** — "the leaf is compact" against "at $M=0.12$" — which is
reading a claim and therefore a **judgement**.* ⇒ **A gate can check a DECLARATION, not a judgement.**
⌗ *And the declaration exists already, unevenly:* ***`COMPUTES:` headers, carried by 39 of 309 receipts*** *— and
`P14_leaf_compactness`'s reads **"on the concrete SdS of B-2 (M=0.12, alpha=1)"**, which is exactly the scope its
citing sentence drops.* **Make it universal and the check becomes mechanical.** *Routed as item 30, **offered not
imposed** — the receipts are the fork's, and this line will not add headers to them.*

⌗ ***Twice now the answer to "what instrument sees this?" has been "none — and the corpus already invented the
convention that would."*** *The first was `\rcpt{}` against quotation-staleness (r2436); this is the second.*

### Revision r2446 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **`scope_table` SHARPENED — three parser defects, each a different reading of "what is a setting", and the finding got STRONGER at every fix.**

*· **TUPLE ASSIGNMENT.** `ombh2, z_rec = 0.0224, 1089.9` matched the `z_rec` pattern and captured **0.0224**, because
the regex takes the first value after the `=` rather than the one **positionally** corresponding to the name.*
⛭ ***AND IT RESOLVED INTO A TRUE POSITIVE ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE FIX:*** *both sites carry real settings — 1089.9
(Set B) and 1100.0 (Set A) — so correcting the parser **added one receipt to each set**.* **A false positive that
becomes a true positive when fixed is the best kind: the tool was seeing something and reporting it under the wrong
name.**
*· **THE NUMBER PATTERN.** `M = sp.Matrix([[0,1,0],...` matched the `M` pattern.* ***A parameter pattern must
require a bare NUMBER, or it reports every use of the letter.***
*· **STRING LITERALS.** P14's second `M` was `det M = +1` **inside a printed label** — which the narrowed number
pattern did not touch, because the text was a perfectly good `"M = +1"`.* ⇒ ***A parameter SETTING is code; a
parameter mentioned in a string is prose the receipt happens to print.*** ⌗ *The same reasoning that already dropped
comments and the docstring — **literals were simply the case nobody had hit.***

rows**. It is now* ***8-versus-7, clean*** *— **a near-even split across P15's receipt layer, which makes "which set
is this number at?" a HARDER question for the paper, not an easier one.*** ⌗ *`M`'s spurious spreads in P07 and P14

### Revision r2410 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **`C2` — THE TWO THREE-NESSES ARE NOT ONE TOWER, and that raises a lemma one level.**

**⌗⌗ THE QUESTION CAME FROM THE TOWER, which is the bake form working.** *`X1r` had established
$\mathrm{Aut}(A_2)=S_3\times\mathbb Z_2$ as a **two-storey tower of covers** — the dial ($6{:}1$, deck $D_6$,
six Nariai **crests**) over the root cover (3 sheets, deck $S_3$, two Nariai **values**), with **$R$ the covering
involution**. `L-212` (r2404) and `C1` (r2408) put a **third** three-fold in play: the turnaround deck, which
**fixes $2M$** and branches at $r=0$.* ***A three-fold that fixes the tower's base is either a further storey, a
parallel cover, or unrelated — and the three are distinguishable.***

**⌗ TWO LINES DECIDE IT.** *With $r$ a root of $r^3-r+2M$:*
$$(\omega r)^3-\omega r+2M \;=\; r^3+2M-\omega r \;=\; r-\omega r \;=\; r(1-\omega),$$
*using $r^3=r-2M$ —* ***which vanishes only at $r=0$.*** ⇒ **The turnaround deck fixes the root cover's base and
does NOT permute its fibre**, *so it is **not a deck transformation of the root cover in any storey**: the two
three-nesses are covers of **different bases with different fibres** (the $2M$-plane with the cubic's roots,
$S_3$, branched at $\lvert r\rvert=\alpha/\sqrt3$; the $r^{D-1}$-plane with the cube roots, $\mathbb Z_3$,
branched at $r=0$).*

**⌗⌗ WHAT IT ADDS, and why it is `4a` and not `4b`.** *P7's `lem:twoturnings` says **no affine change of variable
identifies the horizon roots with the turnaround's** — a statement about **ROOTS**.* ***This is the statement
about COVERS and is strictly stronger: neither three's deck acts on the other's fibre at all, so they cannot be
related by any covering-space construction over the $2M$-plane.*** **The field gave a statement the corpus does
not have**, *which is that bucket's definition — and getting the bucket right is the whole of what makes a
four-bucket ledger worth keeping.*

rotation **carries the same $\alpha$**, so the compact face supplies **no second scale** — which **weakens the
ADD** (nothing is bought to explain a number) **and weakens the DELETE** (if the face carries nothing the
Lorentzian one does not, then treating it as unphysical was not discarding anything).* ⇒ ***The DELETE reading is
NOT YET AVAILABLE, and the work the row owes is to make it available or concede the ADD and price it at the base
rate.***

**⌗ THREE THINGS IT MUST SUPPLY, written into `THE_BASE_RATE` so the argument cannot be made without them:**
*① **what the compact face carries that the Lorentzian one does not** — c54.128 says **not a scale**;*
*② **why treating it as unphysical is a RESTRICTION rather than a READING**, given §1a's adjudication that it is
**real by construction but not a co-equal existent: it carries no clock**;*
*③ **P13's second half** — "a coherent matter route would have to supply **both**".*
⌗ ***That is `L-96`'s standard applied to a new row***: *"what would move it to the favourable side is showing
the adjoint is **already there and was being discarded**, rather than supplying it."*

### Revision r2404 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **`L-212` ANSWERED: NO — all three of the corpus's threes eliminated as sources of a mass grading, in three revisions from discovery to close.**

**⌗⌗ THE DECISIVE FACT WAS IN THE GENERATION INDEX'S OWN DEFINITION.** *P14 `sec:whichthree` seats the
generations on **the turnaround's deck $\mathbb Z_3$**, defined by $\tilde\tau\mapsto\tilde\tau+2\pi i
\alpha/(D-1)$, which* **leaves $r^{D-1}$ INVARIANT while sending $r\mapsto e^{2\pi i/(D-1)}r$** *— and
$r^{D-1}=2M\alpha^{2}\sinh^{2}((D-1)\tilde\tau/2\alpha)$ carries $2M$ as its coefficient.*
⇒ ***So the generation index acts on the RADIUS and FIXES THE MASS PARAMETER exactly.*** **A grading needs the
index to MOVE the graded quantity, and this one does not move $2M$ at all** — *and $2M(\omega r_0)=\omega r_0
-r_0^3$ is neither $2M(r_0)$ nor $\omega\,2M(r_0)$, so there is no character grading either.*

**⌗ ALL THREE THREES, EACH OUT FOR A STATED REASON:**
*· the **horizon** three — move 1 (r2403): **the factorisation singles out nothing**, every root satisfying
$2M=r-r^3$ because that IS the cubic;*
*· the **hinge** three — a **WITHIN-STATE** index by P14's own settlement: **"if the three hinges were the
generations, a bound triple would be one constituent from each generation, which is not what a bound triple of
like constituents is"**, the causal trichotomy of the six hinge-ends forcing one puncture per hinge;*
*· the **turnaround** three — it fixes $2M$.*

**⌗ AND THE CORPUS ALREADY SAID IT IN ITS OWN VOICE**, *which is the third time this front has returned that
shape:* **the deck "says the three are ONE OBJECT READ THREE WAYS and predicts NO MIXING, because it is not a
symmetry that gets broken."** ⇒ ***The answer was latent in the corpus, in a voice the question could not hear.***

**⚠ WHAT IS NOT SHOWN, and must not be read in:** *that no geometric structure could ever bear on fermion masses.
**Only that the three-fold indices the corpus actually HAS do not grade the mass parameter.*** *A5's
flavour-guard stands unchanged either way: **no geometric-quantity = mass identification**.*

**⌗ TWO RECEIPTS, both able to fail:** *`L212_the_factorisation_singles_out_nothing` (14 checks) and

### Revision r2403 — 2026-08-11 (main line). **`L-212`'s FIRST MOVE RETURNS A NEGATIVE THAT REMOVES THE LEVER AND LEAVES THE QUESTION.**

**⌗⌗ THE LEVER WAS P13's FACTORISATION, "singling out $r_0$ — the mass-carrier — against the fundamental pair".**
***It singles out nothing.*** *Every root of $r^3-r+2M$ satisfies $2M=r-r^3$ — **that IS the cubic** — so taking
**any** of the three as $r_0$ reproduces the same factorisation with the other two as the quadratic factor.

negation with **no root fixed as special**.* ⇒ ***The 1+2 split is a CHOICE OF WHICH ROOT IS THE HOLE, not a
distinction the cubic makes.***

**⌗ AND THE CORPUS ALREADY SAID THIS IN ANOTHER VOICE.** *P14/P7's three walls are* **"identical in content,
every root returning the same $2M$, and distinguished by WHICH ROOT EACH TAKES AS ITS HOLE."** ⇒ ***So the
negative is not a surprise to the corpus; it is a surprise to the LEAD*** *— which is exactly the value of
running a first move before building on it, and exactly the shape the entry-point front keeps returning: **the
answer was already in the corpus, in a voice the question could not hear.***

### Revision r2378 — 2026-08-10 (main line). **`RG-1`, THE RETENTION GATE — and the correction of r2377's own reading of it.**

**The correction.** r2377's trail audit reported the working fork's frontier retirements as **exemplary**,
reasoning that nothing had been deleted so the negatives-are-the-map rule was satisfied. **Daryl: that is
wrong, and the correction is a principle rather than a nuance.** *Negatives-are-the-map governs the
**programme's record**. A **published paper** that keeps a paragraph reading "this stood as item one until it
resolved" is not honouring the record — it is reporting its own past ignorance to a reader who came for the
physics.* **What is owed is that the content be folded into the positive syntheses across the papers, and
the stale state struck and moved to `CONSOLIDATE`**, which exists to build the historical status of the
programme and how it developed. The papers present the physics as the finished product.

**The gate, not a ban.** If an account of *how* a problem was worked — including the actual historical
sequencing — is **particularly pedagogical** and worth a paragraph or a section of the paper, it belongs
there. What is refused is grandfathering as a matter of course. **`RG-1` asks one question per site: how
does including this in the final presentation ADD something, in a way that COMPLEMENTS `CONSOLIDATE`'s
description of the same thing in its own framing?** Three dispositions — **FOLD** (default), **MOVE**,
**KEEP** (with its one-sentence answer written into the section). **Guard: nothing is struck until its
content has a home; a MOVE that has not landed is a loss.**

**Opened: [`THE_STAGED_REVISIONS.md`](THE_STAGED_REVISIONS.md)** — the observer line's staging ground.
Revisions prepared in full and **held**, because the working fork is still moving and an edit landed under
it is a merge conflict wearing a fix's clothing. Its law: nothing here has been applied; every entry carries
its gate, locus, done-test and what-it-must-not-do; preparation is not permission; and it is not a second
register — open **questions** go to the lead register, prepared work on **settled** questions lives here.

**First entries.** `SR-1`: the `RG-1` census, **17 sites across four papers** — P7 ×8, p0 ×7, P12 ×1,
P14 ×1, densest in P7's `sec:frontiers` where three retirement paragraphs sit below the list. Five first
dispositions proposed and not applied. `SC-1`: `CONSOLIDATE` has **no section for what `RG-1` will move
into it**, and building one is a precondition for any strike. `SC-2`: the remaining `ARC 14` steps.
`SC-3`: a reporting check so the sweep does not silently recur.

**The misreading is worth the entry on its own.** *A rule correctly held, applied one level off its object,
produced a confident wrong verdict that sounded like discipline — the casebook's exact signature, arriving
in the observer's seat rather than the worker's.*

**⌗ AND THE SAME REVISION EXECUTED IT.** *`SC-1`, `SR-1` and `SC-3` all discharged in the three sessions this
entry covers.*

**`SC-1` — the receiver, and `CONSOLIDATE`'s own placement.** *`RG-1` generalised from a paper rule to a
**placement gate on every document** (Daryl: things are not left lying around, but when worked are homed
appropriately, **at weight**, with an eye to the final places). **Its consequence for sequencing: building a
home and filling it are ONE pass**, because you cannot ask the placement question without deciding where the
thing goes.* **So the same pass built `§16 · THE DEVELOPMENT RECORD`** — the home for what `RG-1` moves, with
its framing fixed as what makes it a *complement* (the paper's framing is the physics; §16's is the

rule.*

Fixed the two printed defects — P3 §449 (called R "the backward-radial reading-swap", wrote it "r↦−r") and §443 (wrote R as bare "r↦−r") — to name R the mass-reflection (r₀↦−r₀, 2M↦−2M). **Verified the §449 R-even/R-odd split symbolically under the corrected R.** Full-corpus scan: no remaining printed spot writes the mass-reflection as bare field "r↦−r" or calls "P" the mass-reflection. So the r1305 phrasing "r₀↦−r₀, hence 2M↦−2M, the field coordinate r held" was incoherent: it split r₀ from r, but r₀ is a value r takes at a horizon — you cannot flip it while holding r. R's coordinate realization is the sweep r↦−r through r=0, which — because the horizons are values of r — drags r₀↦−r₀ and 2M↦−2M onto the conjugate branch (as a symmetry it leaves f invariant; as a grading it is the mass-flip). The real R/P discriminator is whether the **geometry (mass) changes** — R flips it (γ⁵, matter↔antimatter, grades chirality), P is a spatial reflection within one geometry (γ¹γ²γ³, flips chirality) — NOT "which of r/r₀ flips," since r₀ is a value of r. Split reverified symbolically under 2M↦−2M. Card §980 note corrected to match.

1. **The guard that outlives its defect** — worst form, it *dispatches a node to break what is now correct*.
2. **The per-paper one-off** — a symbol defined locally and never promoted while other papers invent their own.
3. **The collapsed definition level** — a geometry-specific value read as a definition, producing phantom clashes.
4. **The ledger that starts defining** — a reporting document drifting into canon.
5. **The reference that names its own reading order incompletely.**
**Plus the pitfalls for whoever works it** — check the level, check the setting, **check whether the defect still exists before treating it** *(three of the six instances were notes about defects already fixed, not defects)*, invent rather than reassign, and **do not annotate the problem area with its own history**.
**How it discharges, and the order matters.** **Continuously by SA-6**, each instance fixed where it lives and recorded here with its pattern — **then the sweep**, once the pattern list is stable, riding the same full-corpus read-through as D.8, D.13 and D.14. *The sweep is the last step, not the first: it can only sweep for patterns the individual cases have taught, which is the order every consolidation arc here has run in.*
**Wired both ways.** The glossary's head now says it holds definitions and not their history, pointing at ARC 9; and **SA-6 now routes every instance, pattern and history to ARC 9 — never into the document that was wrong.**
*No corpus source touched. The reference layer got shorter and more readable, and the record it was carrying got a home that is actively working it.*

### Revision r1620 — 2026-07-24. **The cross-paper receipt fork CLOSED by fixing the tool rather than choosing a workaround. [Daryl-directed: "explain or just pick one."]**
**Daryl was right to call this — I had deferred it three revisions, and it was not a judgement call at all.** The question I kept referring was: P8 cites `\rcpt{order3_bridge}`, registered under P7, and `make_receipt_appendix.py` filtered rows by `paper==scope`, so a standalone P8 build had a marker with no label. **The two options I had been holding out were both workarounds for a gap in the generator**, and each carried its own defect: a hand-added appendix entry drifts from the ledger *by construction* and is destroyed by the next regeneration (which is exactly what happened at r1612, on my own hand), and a duplicate ledger row multiply-defines the label in the book build. *A fork whose branches are all bad is a sign the fork is in the wrong place.*
**The fix.** `make_receipt_appendix.py` now, for a per-paper scope, reads that paper's own `.tex` (comments stripped), collects the `\rcpt{}` stems it actually cites, and includes any ledger row matching a stem it does not own — marked **`[borrowed from Pn]`** so the provenance is on the page. For `corpus` scope it deduplicates by stem, so a receipt cited from several papers appears once in the book appendix. **The ledger remains the single source of truth, which was the premise the tool's own docstring claimed and the old filter quietly broke.**
**Verified, and the workaround retired.** P8 regenerated **from the ledger alone** now reproduces `order3_bridge` (`+1 borrowed: order3_bridge`), so **the hand-restored entry and its r1612 warning comment are deleted** — there is nothing left for a future regeneration to destroy. All sixteen per-paper appendices regenerated; P8 is the corpus's only cross-paper case, which the audit establishes rather than assumes. **Full audit: zero appendix entries anywhere that the ledger cannot generate** (the r1612 landmine class is now empty). **Checker 99 markers ↔ 99 labels, zero dangling, zero duplicate labels in corpus scope and in every per-paper scope.** And **idempotent**: regenerating twice gives a byte-identical file, so the tool can be re-run freely — which is the property the whole "cannot drift" premise needs and did not have.
**Why this and not one of the two.** Both workarounds required a human to remember something the tool should know. The stub required remembering never to regenerate that file; the duplicate row required remembering that the book build would break. **A discipline that depends on remembering a workaround is the quarantine the hard block forbids**, and the r1612 failure is the proof: the thing that got forgotten was forgotten within one revision, by the same reader who had just documented it.
*Cleanup arc CLOSED: Phases 0–5 and every item they turned up. Nothing from the spin-up read remains open.*

Verified `abstract=1, body=1` on every marker. **P3 35pp, 0 undefined; matrix and HTML refreshed; corpus 17/17.**

**★ BAKED into `KICKOFF_ARTHUR`: locate the site by LINE, not by phrase.** `grep -n` the anchor first --- **if it returns two hits, you are about to edit the wrong one.** The body and the abstract carry a claim at **different weights** and want **different sentences**; **a body paragraph pasted into an abstract is not emphasis, it is duplication.** *The masthead check asks whether the abstract lags the body. ### Revision r1143 — 2026-07-17. **The catalogue's shortcut removed — no global constraints; the list is the START, not the result. [Arthur/c43, Daryl-caught.]**

**The gate built the catalogue and immediately tried to shortcut two-thirds of it.** r1142 proposed *"one decision removes ~40 of the 63 at a stroke"* --- strike `Friedmann`/`Robertson`/`Walker`/`Lemaître` corpus-wide as ordinary terms. **Wrong twice over.** *(i)* It **decides from the adjective**: forty sites struck on a **pattern**, with none read --- map-as-territory, the r929 operable-question failure, the r1131 straw man, wearing efficiency. *(ii)* **It would destroy real citations.** Daryl: *"There are times and places to cite their papers."* Friedmann's papers **are** owed a citation somewhere; the question is **where**, and a blanket strike answers it by never asking. **The rule is wrong in both directions at once: it skips the work AND kills the references that are earned.**

**The standard, in Daryl's words, now written into the catalogue:** *"**Meaningful and earned citations. Properly weighed. Every paper checked before it's cited. It has to have a reason not just a name.**"* Unpacked: **earned per site** (the same name earns a citation at one site and none at the next --- both decided by reading the site); **every paper checked before cited** (not the name --- the work, that it says what you cite it for at the weight you cite it at; an unchecked citation is a manufactured receipt); **properly weighed** (a load-bearing lean, a significance-reference and an origin are different citations); and **the strike is a decision, not a default** --- *a strike without a read is the same failure as a citation without a check*.

**What the catalogue is:** *"That gives us a good place to start but we need to do it right not on a few global constraints. **That's the list to start, not the result.**"* --- **the starting list. Sixty-three doors, each opened, read and decided on its own.** There is no shortcut, and its absence is not a defect of the method: **it is the work, and it is why this has lingered a thousand revisions.** The method now reads *paragraph by paragraph* (Daryl's own framing), not entry by entry: the catalogue points at the paper; the paragraph is what gets read.

**The one observation the gather earned --- and its shape is the argument against global rules, not for them:** **`Eddington` is two things in one corpus** --- *Eddington--Finkelstein coordinates* (a named chart, no reference) and **Eddington the person**, whom p0 leans on for the $\Lambda$ argument (*"Eddington's reason $\Lambda$ cannot vanish"*). **Same string, opposite verdicts, decided only by reading the site.**

## The organizing structure — THE CORE THEORY AND ITS APPLICATIONS (the backbone) [recut r532; Daryl-locked]
*The corpus is one story: a complete physical theory developed whole, then applied. Each grouping builds on the ones before; all cross-references are key-based, so the order lives here and in the README spine, not inside the papers.*

- **1 · THE WEDGE [P1].** The crisis result on GR's own terms — the event horizon is a metric singularity, collapse densities never form at finite exterior time. It stands as a GR result alone, and it is the alarm-bells that open the door to everything.
- **2 · THE LOCAL GRAVITATIONAL GEOMETRY [P2–P3].** The local gravitational phenomena and their geometry on the de Sitter substrate: Schwarzschild as a circle (P2 `janzen_circle`), the SdS slicing curve (P3 `SdS-slicing-curve`, the geometric keystone).
- **3 · THE COSMOLOGICAL FORCING, ITS ALGEBRA, AND THE EPISTEMIC GROUND [P4–P6].** Physics-first: what the *observed* world forces, then its algebra, then how it is read. **P4 `modern_parallax`** — the empirical/physics-first foundation: the redshift-isotropy floor forces the cosmic foliation of the existent universe and CR's necessary augmentation of GR (collapsing matter throughout, gravitational entropy toward a final collapsed state — the observed reality that forces the picture). **P5 `groupoid_paper`** — the *algebraic content* of that already-grounded augmentation: the discrete reassignment groupoid (Aut(A₂)=S₃×ℤ₂≅D₆). **P6 `shadow_of_existence`** — the epistemic instrument, the scientific revolution read as theory-choice discipline. *(P4↔P5 swapped r620, physics-first: the empirical forcing precedes its algebra — the groupoid supplies "the algebraic content of the augmentation the foundation establishes"; cross-refs are cite-key based and unaffected.)*
- **4 · THE CORE THEORY [P7–P12] — developed complete, before any application.** The framework (P7 `CR_flatLCDM`: axioms + structured applications + the cosmology-arc synthesis as its pinnacle) → the static theory (P8 `slicing_operator`, matter as the bend of the cut; P9 `range_paper`, the range = GR's whole symmetry-reducible sector, the Carter constant explained as the substrate's surfacing, bounded by the wall) → the temporal pillar (P10 `canonical_time`, the problem of time dissolved, the cosmic clock made a true Hamiltonian) → the motion (P11 `dynamics`, why and how the cut bends in time) → **the keystone that closes it** (P12 `algebroid`: GR's entire constraint algebra *is* the action Lie algebroid 𝔰𝔬(5,1)⋉𝒞 over the substrate — built *from* the operator's anchor, the range's strata, and canonical_time's clock; carrying the discrete A₂/D₆ skeleton and the orientation-parity ℤ₂ that seeds matter). Every structural discovery about GR and CR is placed here — the problem of time, the Carter constant, GR's whole symmetry sector recognised as an action Lie algebroid — and the theory stands complete at the keystone.
- **5 · THE APPLICATIONS [P13–P14, + the fermion frontier].** What the completed theory is applied to: the cosmology (P13 `scalar_perturbations` — the formal cosmological synthesis carried through to the CMB and confronted with data, with P7's pinnacle its conceptual head) and the Standard-Model matter sector (P14 `boundary`), then the unbuilt fermion frontier. The frontier work, correctly placed outside the core theory as its first applications.
- **⬡ THE BOUNDARY PAPER [P0/15] — `geometric_core_paper` ("p0/15"), the border.** Not an interior slot but the frame that *bounds* the whole: **dual** — it STATES the maximally-symmetric substrate (foundational, prior to P1 = the "P0" role) and GATHERS the maximal-symmetry unification (synthetic, posterior to P1–P14, forced by the whole body = the "P15" role). It is built by the reciprocal distillation of the corpus (its landing space fills from each round), so it is forced by P1–P14 by construction — the build method is the evidence. Its foundational content *gathers* the substrate (development lives in P3/thesis), never re-develops it, so the "P0" role forward-references nothing. Held at **hypothesis weight** (r619; the foundational extraction tests it).

> **⚑ THE SPINE IS FLEXIBLE — a living structure, not a fixed ledger.** The order above is the current best topology, drawn from what coheres and what the observed world forces; it is *adjusted as we learn*. The last several turns are the model: the P4↔P5 swap (physics-first forcing), P7's mooted shift (after P4, ahead of P12), the algebroid's keystone lock (r532), and p0/15's emergence as the border all came from coherence and empirical forcings reshaping the order, not from a frozen plan. Cross-references are cite-key based, so reorderings cost only banners + this map + the README spine — which is *why* the spine can stay responsive. Further adjustments are expected (the foundational dependency-extraction, `OPEN_PROBLEMS_MAP`, is the live instrument); nothing here is locked, all stated for reversal.

**The whole is self-similar.** One move recurs at every rung: *find the two things convention has
fused, pry them apart, and the impossibility evaporates* — point≠place (the singularity taxonomy),
synchrony≠simultaneity (cosmic time), occurrence≠existence (the ontology), null≠metrically-degenerate
(the horizon). Including the epistemology that licenses it (P6, the shadow of existence, born where it showed up, after the modern parallax it requires).

**The static↔dynamic hinge survives as a physics fact, not the organizing principle:** P7's reassignment (the Null-Boundary Correspondence) is the *same* horizon under two causal assignments of one ontological layer — collapse (no-formation) ↔ cosmic expansion — foreshadowed in P8's f>0 hole / f<0 cosmos.

Causal/logical order — each builds on the ones before. This is the *causal* order, not any number
printed inside a paper. Status tags mark what is proven vs. the adopted reading vs. the open reach.

1. **`BH_causality_v2.tex`** — *The event horizon is a metric singularity.* The founding result:
   the **Metric Singularity Theorem** (null Δs²=0 + spatial coincidence Δx=0 ⟹ Δτ=0; points stay
